outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a device, a system, a method, a computer program element, and a computer-readable medium for determining spatially dependent x-ray flux degradation and photon spectral change associated with an x-ray tube.

In particular, the invention provides a device configured to determine how the x-ray output of an x-ray tube changes over time or during operation, both in terms of flux intensity and photon spectrum, and to represent these changes in a spatially dependent manner. Such information may be used, for example, for calibration, correction, monitoring, image-quality optimization, dose estimation, or predictive maintenance of x-ray imaging systems.

The device comprises an acquisition unit, a processing unit, a calculation unit, and a combination unit.

The acquisition unit is configured to acquire x-ray flux degradation data for the x-ray tube. The x-ray flux degradation data may represent a reduction or variation in the emitted x-ray flux caused by aging, anode wear, tube usage, thermal loading, contamination, changes in filtration, or other operational effects. The acquired data may be obtained from measurements, calibration scans, detector signals, tube monitoring data, stored reference data, or a combination thereof.

The processing unit is configured to process the acquired x-ray flux degradation data and convert it into spatially dependent flux degradation data. In other words, the processing unit determines how the degradation of the x-ray flux varies across different spatial positions, for example across the x-ray field, detector area, fan angle, cone angle, or irradiation plane. The resulting spatially dependent flux degradation data therefore describes local variations in the x-ray flux degradation rather than merely providing a single global degradation value for the x-ray tube.

The calculation unit is configured to determine a photon spectral change associated with the x-ray tube. The photon spectral change may indicate how the energy distribution of the photons emitted by the x-ray tube has changed, for example due to tube aging, anode surface modification, changes in effective filtration, or changes in the emission characteristics of the tube. The calculation unit further converts the determined photon spectral change into a spatially dependent spectrum. This spatially dependent spectrum represents how the photon energy spectrum varies as a function of spatial position within the x-ray beam or imaging field.

The combination unit is configured to combine the spatially dependent spectrum with the spatially dependent flux degradation data. By combining these two types of information, the device provides a spatially resolved characterization of both the intensity degradation and the spectral modification of the x-ray output. The combined data may therefore describe, for each relevant spatial position, both the amount of x-ray flux degradation and the corresponding change in photon spectrum.

The invention also relates to a corresponding system comprising such a device, for example in combination with an x-ray imaging apparatus or an x-ray tube monitoring arrangement. Furthermore, the invention relates to a corresponding method comprising the steps of acquiring x-ray flux degradation data for an x-ray tube, converting the acquired data into spatially dependent flux degradation data, determining photon spectral change, converting the photon spectral change into a spatially dependent spectrum, and combining the spatially dependent spectrum with the spatially dependent flux degradation data.

In addition, the invention relates to a computer program element which, when executed by a processor, causes the processor to carry out the method described above. The invention further relates to a computer-readable medium having stored thereon such a computer program element.
outputs.L4:
A device, system, and method are provided for determining spatially dependent x-ray flux degradation and photon spectral change in an x-ray tube. In operation, degradation-related data associated with the x-ray tube is acquired, such as measured or modeled information representing changes in x-ray output over different spatial positions. The acquired data is processed to determine how the x-ray flux degradation varies spatially across the x-ray field or across different regions associated with the tube output.

In addition to determining the spatial variation in x-ray flux, the device, system, and method also determine changes in the photon spectrum caused by degradation of the x-ray tube. These spectral changes may be calculated based on the spatial degradation information, tube operating conditions, calibration data, or other characteristics of the x-ray source. The calculated photon spectral changes are then converted into a spatially dependent x-ray spectrum, so that the spectrum is described not merely as a single overall value, but as a function of spatial position.

By combining spatial flux degradation information with spatially dependent spectral information, the resulting characterization provides a more accurate representation of x-ray tube performance. This enables improved modeling, calibration, correction, monitoring, or compensation of x-ray imaging systems, particularly where tube aging, target wear, filtration changes, or other degradation effects cause the x-ray output to vary across space. As a result, the technique supports more precise assessment of x-ray tube behavior and may improve image quality, dose estimation, system calibration, and long-term performance tracking.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, but it has a very important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we may mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that both the speaker and listener understand.

The word “the” brings focus and clarity to a sentence. It can point to something already mentioned, something unique, or something known in context. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky, and we say “the door” when we are talking about a specific door nearby.

Although “the” is short and simple, it is used constantly in everyday English. It helps organize meaning and makes communication more precise. Without it, many sentences would feel incomplete or unclear. In this way, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an invention summary using reference numerals for an x-ray tube monitoring device with units that acquire flux degradation data, process it spatially, calculate spectral change, convert it into a spatially dependent spectrum, and combine the results.
counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Summary

An x-ray tube monitoring device **(100)** is provided for monitoring operational degradation of an x-ray tube **(10)** and estimating spatially dependent changes in an emitted x-ray spectrum. The monitoring device **(100)** includes a flux data acquisition unit **(110)** configured to acquire flux degradation data **(112)** associated with radiation output of the x-ray tube **(10)**. The flux degradation data **(112)** may represent a reduction, variation, or non-uniform change in x-ray flux caused by aging, target wear, anode surface roughening, filtration changes, focal spot drift, or other tube-related degradation mechanisms.

The device **(100)** further includes a spatial processing unit **(120)** configured to process the flux degradation data **(112)** according to spatial position. The spatial processing unit **(120)** may generate spatial degradation information **(122)** that indicates a location-dependent degradation characteristic across a radiation field, detector plane, fan beam, cone beam, or other defined spatial region associated with the x-ray tube **(10)**.

A spectral change calculation unit **(130)** is configured to calculate spectral change information **(132)** based on the spatial degradation information **(122)**. The spectral change information **(132)** may include a change in spectral shape, photon energy distribution, effective energy, beam hardening characteristic, or energy-dependent attenuation behavior corresponding to degradation of the x-ray tube **(10)**.

The monitoring device **(100)** further includes a spectrum conversion unit **(140)** configured to convert the spectral change information **(132)** into a spatially dependent spectrum **(142)**. The spatially dependent spectrum **(142)** represents an estimated x-ray spectrum as a function of spatial position and may define, for each of a plurality of spatial locations **(144)**, a corresponding energy distribution **(146)** of photons emitted by the x-ray tube **(10)**.

A combination unit **(150)** is configured to combine the spatially dependent spectrum **(142)** with one or more additional monitoring results, calibration data, reference spectra, tube operation parameters, detector measurements, or degradation models to generate combined monitoring information **(152)**. The combined monitoring information **(152)** may be used to assess tube condition, compensate image data, update calibration parameters, predict remaining tube life, detect abnormal tube behavior, or generate a maintenance indication.

In some embodiments, the flux data acquisition unit **(110)** obtains the flux degradation data **(112)** from detector measurements, air scans, reference scans, dose sensors, ion chambers, semiconductor sensors, or image-based measurements. In further embodiments, the spatial processing unit **(120)** maps the flux degradation data **(112)** to a two-dimensional or three-dimensional coordinate system corresponding to a detector surface, patient imaging region, or x-ray beam geometry.

In certain embodiments, the spectral change calculation unit **(130)** determines the spectral change information **(132)** by comparing measured flux degradation data **(112)** with baseline flux information **(114)** obtained when the x-ray tube **(10)** is new, calibrated, or in a known reference state. The spectrum conversion unit **(140)** may apply a physical tube model, empirical model, lookup table, machine learning model, or interpolation method to derive the spatially dependent spectrum **(142)** from the calculated spectral change information **(132)**.

The device **(100)** may be implemented as dedicated hardware, software executed by a processor **(160)**, firmware, or any combination thereof. The monitoring device **(100)** may further include a memory **(170)** storing flux degradation data **(112)**, spatial degradation information **(122)**, spectral change information **(132)**, spatially dependent spectra **(142)**, and combined monitoring information **(152)**.

Accordingly, the x-ray tube monitoring device **(100)** enables degradation of the x-ray tube **(10)** to be characterized not only by total flux loss but also by spatially resolved spectral variation, thereby improving calibration accuracy, image correction, quality assurance, and predictive maintenance of x-ray imaging systems.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
